Subject: Re: PrivKit cluster playbook + network walk-through (preflight)

Sara —

Thanks for the checklist and diagram. Quick notes below so we can use the Thursday call for decisions rather than discovery:

1) Node sizing (recommended baseline)
   - Control plane: 3x m4-like instances (or baremetal equivalents) with 32GB RAM, 8 vCPU, SSD; set as dedicated control-plane nodes (taint: node-role=control:NoSchedule).
   - Inference workers: two classes:
     * gpu-infer: 3x nodes per AZ with 8xA100-equivalent GPUs per node for peak throughput (autoscale target pods = 60).
     * cpu-burst: 4x nodes with 192GB RAM and high network I/O for transformer warmup/sidecar workloads.

   - Rationale: keep GPUs in homogenous pools for scheduling/kernels; CPU nodes for pre/post-processing and batching.

2) Storage profile
   - Local NVMe for KV cache and ephemeral token stores. Use the CSI driver with local PVs and a short retention snapshot policy (every 6 hours) to a persistent blockstore for offline recovery.
   - Model artifacts: use a replicated blockstore (Ceph/Rook or cloud block replicated solution). Keep models in blockstore and mount to inference nodes via a read-only PVC with a lifecycle hook that favors layered image-style caching.
   - Backups & eviction: snapshot model artifacts nightly; KV cache eviction TTL 3 hours by default, with a soft-eviction threshold at 70% disk usage.

3) Networking & egress
   - Required outbound endpoints (minimal):
     * api.redwood.example.com:443 (control plane telemetry and rollouts)
     * registry.redwood.example.com:443 (image pulls)
     * metrics.redwood.example.com:9200/443 (optional)
   - Ports: allow 443 outbound from nodes; control plane uses 6443 inbound from cluster peers (internal VPC only).
   - Firewall: restrict Control Plane subnets to only management CIDRs and our peering/VRF. Use NAT for worker egress and maintain an allow-list for third-party telemetry.

4) Upgrades & rollouts
   - Canary model rollout: route 5% traffic to canary model-serving deployment for 24h with automatic rollback on latency or error regressions.
   - Infra patching: rolling reboots across node pool with PodDisruptionBudgets; prefer draining non-GPU nodes first, then GPU nodes with node-slice affinity to keep SLOs.

Next steps prior to call:
   - Karthik: can you validate storage options (Ceph or managed blockstore) for multi-rack replication?
   - PrivKit: confirm target sustained QPS peak and expected model sizes (we used 12–18GB/model in our headcount).

Thanks — happy to jump on Thursday at 10:00 PT if that works. I'll attach a short mutual action plan draft after your confirmation.

—Grace
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Grace / Sara —

Quick storage notes from infra side:

- Ceph/Rook is fine if PrivKit can provision 3-way replication across racks. If the datacenter can't support replication at the block level, recommend using a managed replicated blockstore (our team has a tested pattern for S3-backed model pulls + local caching layer).
- For model distribution: prefetch latest model artifacts to a read-only PVC on inference nodes via an init job that validates checksums. This reduces cold-start spikes and avoids large image pulls at pod start.
- Disk provisioning: separate LV volumes for models vs logs vs cache. Keep cache on fastest tier (NVMe) and set eviction policies in kubelet + CSI for local PV recycling.

Security note (Neha): please confirm that any snapshot replication meets your retention/ER requirements.

Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: PrivKit cluster playbook + network walk-through (preflight)

Sara / team —

Security checklist items to confirm before we go to prod:

- Key management: where will customer KMS live? If PrivKit will manage keys, we need KMIP/HSM integration details and an endpoint for CMK rotation.
- Audit logs: ensure control-plane audit logs are forwarded to PrivKit SIEM over an allow-listed egress channel; retention policy of 365 days minimum.
- Network segmentation: enforce hostNetwork=false for user workloads, and put telemetry/metrics on a dedicated namespace with egress restricted via network policies.
- Data-in-transit: mutual TLS for all internal service-to-service communication.

Action items for our call:
- Grace: bring the minimal egress allow-list (I will confirm exact ports and FQDNs)
- PrivKit: provide KMS endpoint and compliance requirements (SOC2/PCI etc.) so we can map retention and logging SLAs

Thanks —
Neha
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
